title: Fixed and recurring deposits

objectives.text: Compare a fixed deposit with a recurring deposit.
Estimate how compounding affects a deposit's maturity value.
Explain the cost of breaking a deposit early and how to plan around it.

explanation: A fixed deposit puts a lump sum with a bank for a fixed tenure. A recurring deposit puts a fixed amount every month for a fixed tenure. Both pay interest and both are term deposits, but they suit different situations: a fixed deposit suits money you already have, while a recurring deposit builds a corpus from monthly income.

Term deposits usually earn interest that is added to the balance, so the maturity value is higher than principal plus a flat interest figure. The exact method depends on the bank and the tenure. As a rough check, ₹1,00,000 at 7% compounded quarterly for one year grows to about ₹1,07,186, because each quarter's interest starts earning in the next quarter.

The flexibility has a price. RBI's FAME material notes that withdrawing a fixed deposit before the end of its period attracts a penalty. Recurring deposits can also carry conditions for missed instalments. Before you commit, confirm the tenure, the penalty, whether the rate is fixed or floating, and whether you have a nominee. If you may need part of the money, split it across deposits of different tenures rather than locking the whole amount in one.

examples.title: Lump sum versus monthly
examples.text: Priya receives a ₹1,50,000 bonus and puts it in a one-year fixed deposit. Meera, who has no lump sum, starts a recurring deposit of ₹12,500 a month for a year. Both build a deposit corpus, but Priya's money starts earning immediately while Meera's later instalments earn for fewer months.

examples.title: The cost of breaking early
examples.text: Rahul locks ₹80,000 in a two-year fixed deposit, then needs ₹30,000 after eight months for a medical bill. He withdraws part of the deposit and pays the bank's premature-withdrawal penalty, receiving less than the stated rate would suggest. Keeping three months of expenses in a savings account would have avoided that.

keyTakeaways: A fixed deposit takes a lump sum; a recurring deposit takes a fixed monthly amount.
Interest is usually added to the balance, so maturity value reflects compounding.
Premature withdrawal of a fixed deposit normally attracts a penalty.
Split money across tenures so an emergency does not force you to break the whole deposit.

review.notes: Fixed versus recurring deposit descriptions and the premature-withdrawal penalty are checked against RBI FAME 4th edition, Message 2. The ₹1,07,186 figure is a standard quarterly-compounding calculation at 7% for one year, shown as an illustration, not a quoted bank rate. DICGC cover is referenced from the DICGC leaflet. quiz.question: Which deposit suits someone who has no lump sum but can save every month?
quiz.explanation: A recurring deposit accepts a fixed amount each month, which matches regular income. A fixed deposit needs a lump sum at the start.

quiz.question: Why is a deposit's maturity value usually more than principal plus a flat year's interest?
options: Because banks add a random bonus
Because the principal increases every month on its own
Because interest added to the balance earns interest in later periods
quiz.explanation: When interest is credited to the deposit, later interest is calculated on the larger balance. That is compounding, and it raises the maturity value.

quiz.question: What normally happens if you withdraw a fixed deposit before maturity?
options: The bank charges a premature-withdrawal penalty
The bank pays a higher rate as a reward
quiz.explanation: RBI's FAME material states that early withdrawal of a fixed deposit attracts a penalty. That is why money you may need soon belongs in a more accessible account.

disclaimer: General financial education, not personalised advice. Interest rates, compounding methods and penalties differ by bank and product.
